node.title: E1 profile-(2,10) split-prime ideal router
node.closure: local valuation census, residue-degree sieve, and ideal factorization
node.statement: On the binding prize row, every profile-(2,10,S=18) collision has one of ten pure power-of-two cofactors or one of 514, 1028, and 1538. The latter expose one of 128 primes above 257 or 769. Every fixed ideal family contains at most one 256-vector shift/sign orbit, so T_210<=394, |D_210|<=100864, and the coarse edge charge is at most 61906644187645781406222007093836433195008.
node.notes: SPLIT-PRIME FRONTIER 2026-07-29: exact Hasse-derivative enumeration gives mu=1,...,10 and the residue-degree sieve leaves thirteen cofactors. The ten pure families are paid; the remaining problem is occupancy of 384 distinct split-prime families, not unit multiplicity. Charging all 384 is too expensive for the later-profile ledger. No E1 close or Prize movement.
